newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia Oct foreign reserves grow despite aid cuts.
newsitem.headline: Zambia Oct foreign reserves grow despite aid cuts.

text.p: Zambia's October gross foreign reserves rose by more than $34 million to $204.6 million from September's $170.2 million, the central bank said.
It attributed October's reserves growth to continued financial support from multi-lateral donors like the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF).

"The main source of the increase in the gross international reserves position...was the World Bank's disbursement of $44.8 million and purchases of $16.1 million from the market," central bank spokesman Dave Kalumba told Reuters in an interview.
World Bank and IMF aid more than countered aid cuts by bilateral donors from western countries displeased with the government's constitutional reforms earlier this year, it said.
Constitutional reforms earlier this year banned certain candidates from contesting presidential elections, which were held on November 18.

London-based Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) estimates bilateral donors withheld at least $100 million in balance of payment support this year, and predicts that normal aid flows will not resume in the near future.

"The government's stubbornness over the electoral regulations make it increasingly unlikely that the constitutional issues surrounding candidacy rules will fade from bilateral donors' memories after the poll and that they will swiftly resume their support.
"It appears more probable that Zambia has lost its position as a major bilateral aid recipient," the EIU fourth quarter country report on Zambia said.
The report, however, said multilateral donors are unlikely to respond to western governments' pressure and suspend their programmes in Zambia over concerns on its governance record.
